svg.title: SPI bus timing
svg.desc: SPI timing of the MAX22200 in mode 0 for a Command Register write: CMD high frames the transfer, CSB low frames the byte, SDI is read on each rising SCK edge and the open-drain SDO shifts the fault byte out.
svg.text: SPI mode 0 (CPOL 0, CPHA 0). Datasheet: Electrical Characteristics (SPI
Specifications), p. 10; Command Register Description (COMMAND), p. 25;
CMD setup time before CSB falls
CSB fall to the first SCK rise
SDO propagation delay (310 Ω and 20 pF to 3.3 V)
CMD high for the whole transfer writes the Command Register; CMD low
accesses the register it selected. The SPI Detailed Description says the
interface can operate up to 5 MHz; the table's 100 ns period allows 10
MHz. SDO is open drain: its rising edge depends on the pull-up and the
